title: Timeline curation and span-healing for VPC/on-prem observability collectors
creator: Priya Singh
description: Problem: For dedicated and private deployments we regularly see partial trace trees when collectors drop spans during transient backpressure, network blips, or when local buffering overflows. This causes spike artifacts in latency and error dashboards and high false-positive regression alerts. Goal: implement a reconciliation + span-healing pipeline at the collector/edge level that 1) detects gaps in trace timelines, 2) curates a canonical timeline for downstream consumers (metrics, logs, tracing backends), and 3) supports eventual replay/healing for short retention windows without impacting latency SLOs for live requests.
acceptance_criteria: Collector identifies >90% of trace gaps caused by out-of-order or missing span arrivals in canary environment
Canonical timeline output reconciles span parent-child relationships and reduces orphan spans by >= 80% in on-prem test datasets
No additional tail latency > 50ms p95 introduced to synchronous agent forwarding in Dedicated tier under normal load
Feature toggles to disable healing per-customer and per-cluster must exist and be respected by control plane
End-to-end integration test and chaos scenario in staging that injects 10% packet loss and validates repair behavior
plan_steps: Design: define reconciliation model (watermark + short-lived buffer + causal window) and healing heuristics (parent inference, timestamp smoothing)
Collector change: add ephemeral timeline buffer with configurable window (default 30s) and an index by trace-id + sequence heuristic
Control plane: expose per-tenant toggles and buffer sizing via config API; add limits so on-prem clusters can't exceed node memory cap
Downstream: emit a reconciliation metadata envelope alongside healed traces (fields: reconciliation_version, gaps_detected, heuristic_score)
Dashboarding: new latency/error dashboards that separate raw ingest vs reconciled metrics and visualize healed-span counts
Rollout: dev -> alpha (internal clusters) -> canary (3 customers on Dedicated) -> gradual rollout with rollback criteria
technical_notes: We considered CRDT-based approaches but rejected them for 30s windows due to added complexity and write amplification on local disk

Chosen approach: lease-less ephemeral buffer with periodic watermarking. Each collector keeps a sliding window keyed by trace-id; an 'emit' watermark moves forward using max observed event time minus safety margin
Span parent inference: prefer explicit parent_id; fall back to timestamp-first-child heuristic + service affinity when parent is missing
Backpressure behavior: when buffer exceeds memory threshold, policy=evict-oldest with tombstoning to avoid reintroducing known gaps
Security: reconciled envelopes are tenant-scoped and signed with collector identity; no cross-tenant inference allowed
Telemetry: new counters (reconciled_spans_total, gap_detected_total, heuristic_applied_total), histograms for repair latency, and a gauge for buffer memory usage
